scope: Matched two/four shard manual CI, including the complete qualification workload at the workflow configuration used during issue #407 implementation.
path_convention: All paths are repository-relative. <REPO> denotes a checkout root. Raw machine logs and full per-test records remain ignored under build/validation/fix-issues/20261118-ci-efficiency/.
commands: git switch fix/407-measured-ci-shards  # source ad55248131be0e5f9a0344e6662d0ed0b160d4cb at dispatch
gh workflow run ci.yml --repo MOMA-AUH/gwflow --ref fix/407-measured-ci-shards -f shard-count=2
gh workflow run ci.yml --repo MOMA-AUH/gwflow --ref fix/407-measured-ci-shards -f shard-count=4
gh run download RUN_ID --repo MOMA-AUH/gwflow --name gwflow-ci-runtime --dir build/validation/fix-issues/20261118-ci-efficiency/407-runtime-COUNT
command_placeholders: RUN_ID is 44371388219 for COUNT=2 or 44371404467 for COUNT=4. The branch must still point at the recorded source when reproducing these dispatches.

timing_definitions.runner_seconds: Sum completed_at minus started_at for every allocated non-skipped job, including classification, build, fixture preparation, pip/compatibility, suites, real acceptance, aggregate, transfers, cleanup, and required gates. No queue time or per-job billing rounding.
timing_definitions.elapsed_seconds: Latest completed_at minus earliest started_at across those jobs. Includes dependency and inter-job scheduling waits. Initial dispatch queue time is separate.
timing_definitions.whole_job_stage_seconds: Disjoint job groups that sum exactly to runner_seconds.
timing_definitions.test_execution_seconds: Sum monotonic per-test durations from all passing shard records. This is a subset of suite execution-step and whole-job time.
timing_definitions.overlapping_details: suite_restore_and_fixture_transfer_seconds and standalone_artifact_action_seconds are diagnostic subsets of whole jobs. Composite restore includes embedded runtime/image download and cache transfer. Never add these subsets again to runner_seconds.

coverage.every_run: 1126 discovered tests, each exactly once across its expected count; zero failures and zero skipped tests. Exact runtime identity checked before/after every shard and by the coverage aggregate.
coverage.release_process: Both workflow_dispatch runs forced full simulations. Fresh-cache qualification, independent profile/replacement comparisons, bundle verification and both required gates passed.
coverage.retries: Both samples are attempt 1 with no retries. Fail-fast remains false. Focused regressions verify deterministic plans/assignments, independent retry membership, and missing/duplicate/count rejection.

cross_run_environment.explanation: The independent builds produced different candidate package checksums. Each run enforced its own exact candidate artifact and identical dependencies in all shards. This compares the same source/workload, not a shared candidate binary across runs.

limitations: One sample per count, run concurrently on independent hosted machines. Between-run variance and a confidence interval cannot be estimated.
Identical runner labels/image versions do not control host hardware, region, network, scheduler or package-service conditions.

Two-shard test execution totaled 3075.677 seconds versus 3626.724 with four. These samples do not identify how much of this difference is caused by shard count; it contributes to the observed cost difference.
Cache availability, composite restoration delays, artifact transfers and all final simulations remain included. No synthetic timing replaces the measured full workloads.
The provisional pre-1.0 source compatibility check ran. Stable preserved-release comparison steps were inapplicable under the checkout-pinned descriptor, not skipped required application coverage.
These observations apply to this source and environment. No generic cost saving, feedback SLA or tight CI timing threshold follows from them.

selection.balancing: Existing deterministic SHA-256 assignment by test identity.
selection.rationale: Choose the lower observed allocation cost for this CI-efficiency goal. Two shards took about 39 minutes instead of 30, near the 38.4-minute complete pipeline already observed earlier in the same queue. This accepts slower feedback for fewer replicated setup jobs and lower measured runner allocation. One sample does not establish a guaranteed reduction.
selection.balance_rationale: Timing-aware redistribution can shorten the longest shard but does not remove test work. Historical predictions suggested only a few minutes of benefit and require a maintained timing baseline. Keep the simpler stable assignment and remeasure before adding that policy.
